title: How each pauri sums up
hookLine: each pauri gathers the saloks before it into a stanza of its own

lines: A STEP DOWN TO THE WATER.
cards: Climb the steps down to the water at a gurdwara sarovar, or a staircase in an old Punjabi house, and every step has a name: pauri. The same word means a ladder rung.
It's also the name of the stanzas you've been hearing for weeks without quite noticing them. Japji is built of pauris. So is every var in the Guru Granth Sahib.
For three weeks we've mostly listened to saloks, the short verses about trees, threads and scales. Today, the steps they sit on.

teach.h: A VAR: A BALLAD OF HEROES.
teach.b: A var, as we heard on day five hundred thirty-six, is an old Punjabi ballad form, sung about heroes and battles. Its stanzas are pauris, and in a var they march: each one a step forward in the story.
The Guru Granth Sahib has twenty-two vars.
In the Asa di Var, the pauris are Guru Nanak's, twenty-four of them, and they carry the main line of the poem: who the One is, how creation stands, what a true servant is like, what the Guru does.
In front of each pauri sit two or more saloks, some Guru Nanak's, some Guru Angad's.
Many scholars hold that they were set beside the pauris when Guru Arjan compiled the Granth, gathered by theme to open up the step that follows.
So the saloks wander: a silk-cotton tree, a cartload of books, a thread, a kitchen. They make you see something. Then the pauri arrives and gathers what you've seen into one step forward.
You've felt this already. The pauri where Guru Nanak says he's a sacrifice to the True Guru, who put wisdom on his eyes, came after saloks about show without substance.
The saloks showed the problem; the pauri named the turning.
Hear the Asa di Var sung and you can feel the rhythm: wander, gather; wander, gather.
Many small pictures, then one step up. It's a way of learning that doesn't rush. You don't climb the whole staircase at once.

how: When Asa di Var is sung at dawn, ragis sing the saloks and then each pauri, and many Sikhs read the var from a gutka, pauri by pauri.

games.q: you've just heard two saloks about a tall, useless tree and empty bowing. what comes next in the var?
o: another salok on a new topic.
a pauri that gathers them into one step forward.
games.why: the pauri arrives: a sacrifice to the True Guru, who put wisdom on the eyes. the saloks show; the pauri gathers.

practice: If you have a gutka or an app with the Asa di Var, read one pauri slowly, all the way through, in Gurmukhi or in translation.

If not, hold the pauri from this week in mind: the contented ones served, did good, ate little, broke the world's chains, and the One kept giving more; let it sit as one step, complete, and breathe with it.
If you pray, you can say Waheguru at the end.
